bull.b: Strong quarterly growth, recovery in tissue-based testing, and the ExoDx integration support sustained expansion in the molecular diagnostics franchise. Reiterated guidance indicates management expects commercial momentum to continue through 2026.

bull.t: Healthy gross margins and improving operating leverage
bull.b: Gross margins above 60% indicate attractive underlying test economics and provide a foundation for future operating leverage. As revenue scales and integration costs normalize, this margin profile could help move the business toward adjusted EBITDA profitability.

bull.t: Clinical evidence and prostate diagnostics positioning
bull.b: Peer-reviewed evidence and ongoing clinical visibility can strengthen physician confidence, reimbursement discussions, and adoption of prostate cancer tests. This supports differentiation in a specialized market and may expand the long-term commercial value of the product portfolio.

bear.b: The company remains materially unprofitable despite revenue growth, and acquisition-related expenses have widened losses. Until recurring revenue growth translates into positive EBITDA and net income, internal funding capacity and financial resilience remain limited.

Higher debt combined with negative equity increases refinancing, covenant, and dilution risks. This constrains strategic flexibility and leaves the company more dependent on successful commercialization or additional capital to meet obligations over the medium term.

bear.t: Negative cash generation and capital dependence
bear.b: Improved cash-burn trends are not yet sufficient to make the business self-funding. Continued negative free cash flow means available liquidity can be consumed before profitability arrives, preserving the risk of further financing, dilution, or reduced investment.
